title: Cell Biology Adventure 1: Prokaryotes vs Eukaryotes
welcome_lead: Today you'll compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells — the two great lineages of life.
meta_desc: Biology Cell Biology — prokaryote vs eukaryote structure, organelles, size and surface-area-to-volume.
final_note: You learned that prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles, eukaryotes have a nucleus and ER, and small cells maximise SA:V.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Life splits into two cellular architectures.

Prokaryotes (1-5 μm) — no nucleus, circular DNA in nucleoid, 70S ribosomes, peptidoglycan cell wall.

Eukaryotes (10-100 μm) — true nucleus, linear DNA on histones, 80S ribosomes, ER, Golgi, mitochondria.

Nature of science: electron microscopy (Palade, 1950s) revealed ultrastructure invisible to light microscopes.

As a cell grows, volume rises as r³ but surface area only as r².

For a cube of side L: SA = 6L², V = L³, so SA:V = 6/L.

If diffusion supplies O₂ and removes CO₂, large cells starve. Solutions: stay small, flatten (e.g. erythrocytes), or fold the membrane (microvilli).

Not all cells fit the textbook plan:

- Striated muscle fibres — multinucleate, formed by cell fusion.
- Aseptate fungal hyphae — long tubes of shared cytoplasm.
- Red blood cells — anucleate at maturity; cannot divide.

This challenges the strict 'cell theory' that all life is built of discrete cells.
